scope: Security-sensitive and multi-table mutations are atomic under PostgreSQL (and SQLite). Failure is injected between statements and partial state must never commit. Deliberately non-atomic external effects are documented.

entries.atomicity: Administrator insert is transactional and guarded by a PostgreSQL advisory lock (single-winner). Session issuance is a post-commit convenience: if its insert fails after the admin commit, the admin exists and can sign in; no data-loss or privilege issue. Documented minor non-atomicity.
Atomic after CP4 repair: the session and its short-lived access token commit in one transaction; a failed access insert rolls back the session, leaving no orphaned row.
Atomic after CP4 repair: revoke-old + insert-new session + access token commit in one transaction; a failed access insert leaves the original refresh token valid (no partially consumed rotation).
Single-statement insert; atomic by the engine.
Transactional: metadata, field rows and the physical table create or roll back together.
Transactional: physical table dropped and metadata deleted in one transaction; dependent rows are removed by foreign-key cascade.
Transactional metadata plus safe create/copy/validate/swap of the physical table with rollback on incompatible data.
Transactional: delete + reinsert of the rule set commit together.

entries.mutation: record create/update/delete with audit, event and outbox
entries.atomicity: Transactional and composed: record, durable event, audit fact and any required outbox job commit together; rollback produces no event, audit fact or provider call.
Transactional: a 1,000-record batch commits or rolls back as a whole.

Bytes are written to storage before metadata insert (deliberately non-atomic external effect); a failed metadata insert triggers a compensating storage delete. Quota and staging are handled before publication.

Metadata delete is deferred inside a transaction until the storage delete succeeds; a failed storage delete rolls back and preserves metadata. BeginTx/Commit errors are currently ignored (documented hardening item).
Single-statement insert/update with in-process secret encryption; atomic by the engine.
Single-statement insert/update; atomic by the engine.
Transactional claiming; PostgreSQL uses FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED, SQLite serializes. One execution per successful claim; leases recover after expiry.
All-or-nothing transactional import into an initialized empty destination; a failed import leaves the destination unchanged.

deliberatelyNonAtomicExternalEffects: remote webhook delivery may already have received a request before a later failure; deliveries are job-driven and retried with idempotency keys
Lambda invocation is asynchronous and job-driven; provider acceptance may precede completion
file bytes are written to object storage before metadata publication; compensating cleanup removes bytes if metadata binding fails
first-administrator session issuance follows the admin commit as a convenience
knownHardeningItems: files.remove ignores BeginTx/Commit errors (should fail closed)
adminauth setup issues the session after the admin commit (convenience, documented)
